## FAQ

### Why fiberglass

Q: Why choose a fiberglass pool over concrete or vinyl liner?
A: Fiberglass is the fastest of the three to install, needs the least upkeep and rarely carries a big future repair bill, which is why many Jacksonville families choose it. The one-piece shell is made in a factory and set in weeks rather than months. Its smooth, non-porous gelcoat gives algae less to grip, so it typically needs fewer chemicals and less brushing. Concrete is the better answer when you need a truly custom shape, and vinyl usually has the lowest upfront price. See the full comparison guide.

Q: Is fiberglass good for Florida's soil, high water table and hurricanes?
A: Yes, a fiberglass pool suits Northeast Florida when it is installed for the site's soil and groundwater. iTop Pools in Jacksonville checks access and soil on the site visit and plans the set around local conditions. One rule matters above all: never drain a fiberglass pool yourself, because high groundwater after heavy rain can push an empty shell upward. Before a storm, leave the pool full and follow the Pool School storm guidance.

Q: What pool types and materials do you work with?
A: Fiberglass and concrete/gunite, plus paver decks, water features and outdoor kitchens. All built to take Florida sun, rain and daily use without looking tired in five years.

### Cost & financing

Q: How much does a fiberglass pool cost in Jacksonville, compared with concrete and vinyl liner?
A: A typical installed fiberglass pool runs about $58,000–$85,000, compared with about $78,000–$110,000 for concrete and about $40,000–$65,000 for vinyl liner. These are published ranges, before deck, enclosure and fencing, and they vary with size, site and features. iTop Pools gives you a firm written price after the site visit. Build your own estimate to see how the pieces add up.

Q: What is the total cost including deck, screen enclosure and fencing?
A: Your total depends mostly on deck size and material, whether you add a screen enclosure, and how much access your yard allows. Florida also requires a pool safety feature, which is included in iTop's permitting plan. Because each yard differs, we measure first and then give you one written price covering the pool, deck, enclosure and permits. The estimator shows which choices move the number most.

Q: Why are your prices better than other builders I've quoted?
A: Because we don't subcontract. Most builders hire out the shell, the deck and the pavers, and each layer adds its own markup. We have our own specialized crew for all of it, so you pay for the work instead of the middlemen.

Q: Do you offer financing?
A: Most homeowners finance at least part of a pool, usually through an unsecured pool loan, a home equity loan, a HELOC or a cash-out refinance. Rates and terms depend on the lender and your credit, so talk to iTop about your options when we go through your price. Our financing guide compares all four in plain English.

### Fiberglass vs concrete vs vinyl

Q: Which pool type costs least to own over 25 years?
A: Fiberglass usually has the lowest long-term ownership cost, because it avoids the two largest recurring bills: concrete resurfacing and vinyl liner replacement. Vinyl liners commonly need replacing every 10–15 years at about $3,000–$7,500 each, and Florida's sun can shorten that. Concrete needs periodic resurfacing and generally more chemicals. Actual costs depend on the pool and how it is cared for.

Q: When is concrete a better choice than fiberglass?
A: Concrete is the better choice when you want a vanishing edge, an unusual size or a shape no mold offers. Expect a longer build and periodic resurfacing over the pool's life. If your yard truly needs something custom, iTop will tell you so.

### Installation & permits

Q: How long does a pool take, start to finish?
A: Once permits and HOA approvals are finalized, Barrier Reef puts a typical fiberglass install at 2–6 weeks, depending on size, site and weather. Our crew isn't split across other companies' jobs, which is why we can move faster than most. You'll get a firm timeline before we break ground.

Q: Do I need permits, and will you handle them?
A: Yes, and yes. HOA approvals, engineering and county permitting are all ours to chase, including the safety feature Florida law requires. You don't fill out a form or make a phone call.

Q: Who is actually on my property during the build?
A: Our own crew: the same specialized team on every iTop job, for both pools and pavers. No rotating subcontractors, no one you haven't met and no finger-pointing when something needs fixing.

Q: Will weather push my timeline?
A: Heavy rain can move a day here and there. We tell you when it happens instead of going quiet, and we keep the schedule moving around it.

### Maintenance

Q: How much maintenance does a fiberglass pool need?
A: A fiberglass pool needs less routine care than concrete or vinyl: mostly skimming, keeping the water balanced and standard equipment servicing. We build for low upkeep, and we walk you through exactly how to run it before we hand it over. Keep the water chemistry in range, because the finish warranty assumes it. Pool School has seasonal care guides written for Northeast Florida.

Q: Will my pool be a lot of work to maintain?
A: We build for low upkeep. Routine cleaning and standard servicing are all it takes, and we walk you through exactly how to run it before we hand it over.

Q: Do you offer energy-efficient options?
A: Yes. Options like salt systems, variable-speed pumps and automation can cut running costs. We'll tell you which ones actually pay for themselves in your setup.

Q: Can I get a tanning ledge, spa, heater or salt system?
A: Yes, iTop Pools can build a tanning ledge, spa, heater or salt system into your project. Several Barrier Reef shells already have a built-in lounging ledge or integrated spa, and separate spas, sundecks and tanning ledges can be added to many models. Heat pumps, salt systems, LED lighting and automation are also available. Filter the model finder by feature to see which shells include them.

### Warranty

Q: What does the Barrier Reef warranty cover?
A: Barrier Reef provides a Lifetime Limited Structural Warranty on the shell, transferable once, plus a 15-year finish warranty against blistering. iTop separately warrants our installation work, and pumps, heaters and automation carry their own manufacturers' warranties. The written warranty documents govern. See who covers what.

A: A site visit, real measurements and a 3D design of your backyard, at no cost and with no obligation. You see exactly what you're buying before you commit a dollar. Book your free visit.

Q: Can I see a pool you already built?
A: Yes. Browse our work, or ask us and we'll arrange a visit to a finished project near you. We'd rather you stand next to the real thing.

## Guides

### Fiberglass vs concrete vs vinyl: which suits Florida?
Key takeaways Fiberglass is typically installed in 2–6 weeks, concrete in 3–6 months. Fiberglass has a smooth, non-porous surface and rarely carries a big future cost. Choose concrete for a truly custom shape, and vinyl for the lowest upfront price. Almost every Jacksonville buyer starts with the same question: which type of pool? All three can be great. They just suit different priorities. How do fiberglass, concrete and vinyl compare? Compare Fiberglass Concrete Vinyl liner Typical install 2–6 weeks 3–6 months Several weeks Surface Smooth gelcoat Plaster or pebble, textured Soft vinyl Shape freedom Choose from molds Any shape Many shapes Big future cost Rare Resurfacing Liner replacement Why is fiberglass popular in Florida? A fiberglass shell is made in a factory and set in one piece, so the build is short and less weather-dependent. That matters in a Florida summer. The gelcoat surface is smooth and non-porous, which gives algae less to grip. Barrier Reef estimates vinyl pools use about 50% more chemicals than fiberglass. When does concrete make sense? If you want a vanishing edge, an unusual size or a shape no mold offers, concrete (gunite) is the answer. Expect a longer build and periodic resurfacing over the pool's life. Where does vinyl fit? Vinyl usually has the lowest upfront price. Barrier Reef puts fiberglass at roughly 15–20% more than vinyl. The liner wears and needs replacing, which industry guides put at around every 10 years. Our take: for most Northeast Florida families who want to swim this season and spend weekends swimming rather than scrubbing, fiberglass is the best balance. If your yard needs something truly custom, we'll tell you. Sources: Barrier Reef Pools USA FAQ (install time, chemical use, price vs vinyl); published industry comparison guides (concrete build time, liner life).

### Rectangle, freeform or kidney? Picking a shape
Key takeaways Rectangles give the most usable swimming length and suit modern homes. Freeform curves feel like a resort and blend with natural stone and palms. Kidney and plunge shapes suit lanai corners and townhome lots. Shape is mostly about how you'll use the water and what your house looks like. Who should choose a rectangular pool? Clean lines suit modern and transitional homes. They also give the most usable swimming length, so they're great for laps. Try the Aussie, Bondi or Whitsunday. Who should choose a freeform pool? Curves feel like a resort and blend with palms and natural stone. Try Coral Sea or Billabong Cove. Who should choose a kidney or plunge pool? Soft, classic and compact. Kidney shapes wrap nicely around a lanai corner, and plunge pools fit townhome lots. Try Opal or Milano. Not sure? Take the 30-second pool finder on our homepage, or drop any model into the 3D studio and walk around it.

### What does a fiberglass pool cost in Jacksonville?
Key takeaways National guides put an installed fiberglass pool at roughly $50,000–$150,000. Shell, features, deck, site and enclosure drive the final number. A bid that leaves items out isn't cheaper, it's incomplete. The honest answer is that it depends on the shell, the features, the deck and your site. Here's how to think about it. What do fiberglass pools cost nationally? National industry price guides put an installed fiberglass inground pool at roughly $50,000 to $150,000. In Florida, advertised fiberglass packages often start in the $40,000s before decking, screens and upgrades. What changes the price? Shell size and model. Longer and deeper shells cost more to make, ship and set. Features. Spa, heat pump, lighting, automation and water features. Deck. Square footage and material (pavers, travertine or porcelain). Site. Access, soil, slope, and whether a crane is needed. Screen enclosure. Common in Northeast Florida, and a significant line item. What should a complete quote include? Shell, delivery, excavation and haul-off, set and leveling, plumbing and equipment, backfill, coping, deck, electrical bonding, permits, the safety feature Florida requires, and start-up. If a bid is missing items, it isn't cheaper. It's incomplete. Use our estimator to get a realistic range in two minutes, then book a free site visit for a firm, written price. Source: published national fiberglass pool price guides. Ranges vary by region and project.

### Permits, HOAs and Florida pool safety rules
Key takeaways Every inground pool in Northeast Florida needs a building permit. Most neighborhoods also need HOA approval, and iTop handles both. Florida law requires a new residential pool to have at least one approved safety feature. Every inground pool in Northeast Florida needs a building permit, and most neighborhoods also need HOA approval. iTop handles both. Do I need a building permit? Your city or county reviews the site plan, setbacks, electrical and drainage before work starts, then inspects during the build. Will my HOA need to approve it? Many communities, including Nocatee, Julington Creek and Ponte Vedra neighborhoods, want drawings, materials and sometimes colours before approving. Our 3D design and site plan make this faster. What does Florida's pool safety law require? Florida's Residential Swimming Pool Safety Act (Chapter 515, Florida Statutes) requires a new residential pool to have at least one approved safety feature. Options include a compliant barrier or fence, an approved safety cover, exit alarms on doors and windows that open to the pool, or self-closing, self-latching doors. We'll recommend the safety option that fits your family and your county's inspection, and build it into your quote. Requirements vary by jurisdiction. Your permit reviewer has the final word.

### Pool financing 101
Key takeaways The four common routes are a pool loan, home equity loan, HELOC and cash-out refinance. Loans secured by your home usually carry lower rates, but put the home at risk. iTop isn't a lender, so talk to a lender or advisor before you choose. Most families finance at least part of a pool. These are the four common routes. 1. Unsecured pool loan A personal loan made for home projects. It's fast, and your house isn't collateral, but rates are usually higher. 2. Home equity loan A fixed amount borrowed against your equity. It usually carries a lower rate, but your home secures it. 3. HELOC A line of credit you draw as the build progresses. Rates are often variable. 4. Cash-out refinance You replace your mortgage with a larger one. This can make sense when current rates are at or below your existing rate. Try different down payments and terms in our estimator. Talk to a lender or financial advisor before you choose. iTop isn't a lender.

### How to choose a finish colour
Key takeaways Barrier Reef's US range has seven finishes. Light finishes give turquoise water, and dark finishes look deeper and more reflective. Depth, shade and deck color all change how the water looks. Barrier Reef's US range has seven finishes: Aquamarine, Arctic, California, Evening Sky, Ocean, Sandstone and Silver Mist. Should I choose a light or dark finish? Light finishes such as Arctic and Sandstone give turquoise, Caribbean-style water. Dark finishes such as Ocean and Evening Sky look deeper and more reflective, like a lake. What changes the color of the water? Depth. The deep end always reads darker than the steps. Sky and shade. A screen enclosure softens and darkens the water slightly. Deck. Light travertine makes water look brighter. Charcoal pavers make it look moodier. Compare any two finishes side by side in our colour lab, then ask us to bring real samples to your site visit.

### Tanning ledges, spas and lighting: what's worth it?
Key takeaways A tanning ledge is one of the upgrades owners use most. Heat pumps suit Florida's mild winters and stretch the swim season. Lighting and automation are cheap during the build and awkward to add later. Some upgrades get used every day. Others get forgotten. Here's what we see owners use most. Is a tanning ledge worth it? A shallow shelf, usually under a foot of water. It's where chairs, toddlers and morning coffee end up. Highly recommended. Should I add a spa? Choose a shell with an integrated spa, like Sydney Harbour, or add a raised spillover spa. Great for cooler months. Do I need a heat pump? Florida's mild winters suit heat pumps well, and they stretch your swim season. Are LED lighting and automation worth it? Colour LEDs and phone control for pump, lights and heat. Cheap to add during the build and awkward to add later. Toggle a spa and tanning ledge in the 3D studio to see the difference, then price them in the estimator.

### Your build, week by week
Key takeaways Barrier Reef puts a typical install at 2–6 weeks once permits and HOA approval are in hand. The shell arrives in one piece and is backfilled evenly while the pool fills. Weather, inspections and enclosure lead times can change the timeline. Once permits and HOA approval are in hand, a fiberglass install moves quickly. Barrier Reef puts a typical install at 2 to 6 weeks. Layout & locates. We mark the pool and call Sunshine 811 so utilities are located. Excavation. Usually a day or two, with soil hauled away. Delivery & set. The shell arrives in one piece and is lowered, leveled and plumbed. Backfill. We backfill evenly while the pool fills with water, to keep pressure balanced. Coping, deck & enclosure. The same crew lays the deck. Inspections. Final electrical and safety-feature inspections. Start-up & handover. We balance the water and show you how everything works. Timeline varies with weather, inspections, site conditions and screen-enclosure lead times.

### Site access: how a shell gets into your yard
Key takeaways Shells arrive on a truck in one piece, so the route into your yard matters. Many pools can be set from the side, and fence panels can be removed and replaced. Narrow lots or pools behind the house may need a crane. Fiberglass shells arrive on a truck in one piece, so the route into your yard matters. Can the shell come through my side yard? If there's a clear path wide enough for equipment, we can usually set the shell from the side. Fence panels can be removed temporarily and replaced. When is a crane needed? Pools behind the house, narrow lots or screened areas may need a crane to lift the shell over. It's common, quick, and priced into your quote up front. What do we check on the site visit? Gate and side-yard widths Overhead lines and trees Septic, irrigation and drainage Slope and soil

### Your first 30 days as a pool owner
Key takeaways Run the pump as instructed and brush the walls and floor in week one. Typical targets are pH 7.4–7.6, free chlorine 1–3 ppm and alkalinity 80–120 ppm. A weekly routine takes about 10 minutes. We'll start your pool and walk you through everything, but here's what to expect. What happens in week one? Run the pump as instructed, brush the walls and floor, and keep children's toys out until the water is balanced. What should my water levels be? pH: about 7.4–7.6 Free chlorine: about 1–3 ppm Total alkalinity: about 80–120 ppm Your handover sheet lists the exact targets for your pool and equipment. Saltwater systems still produce chlorine, so test just the same. What is the weekly routine? Skim, empty baskets, test, adjust, and give the floor a quick brush. The smooth gelcoat makes this the easy part.

### Hurricane prep for your pool
Key takeaways Never drain a fiberglass pool, because high groundwater can push an empty shell up. Don't restart equipment until it's dry and debris is cleared. Call iTop after the storm if anything looks off. Northeast Florida storms are part of life. Here's how to prepare your pool. Do Keep the pool full. The water's weight helps hold the shell in place. Turn off pump, heater and lights at the breaker. Bring in furniture, toys and loose décor. Raise chlorine slightly before the storm. Don't Never drain a fiberglass pool. High groundwater after heavy rain can push an empty shell up. Don't restart equipment until it's dry and debris is cleared. After the storm, call us if anything looks off. We'd rather check than have you guess.
